- Model tends to overestimate prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast often peaks too early or too high, then underestimates the subsequent correction or mean reversion.
- Model underestimates the true price in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, particularly when true values show upward momentum.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in capturing the true price trend, especially when the true price rises sharply after a dip.
- When the true price exceeds the model’s forecast by more than 5% in the first 5 days, model tends to overcorrect later, underestimating the true value.
- Model frequently fails to account for mean reversion in the final 10 days, leading to underestimation of true values.
- Model tends to overestimate prices in the middle of the forecast (days 15–25) when true values are often lower or show downward correction.
- Model underestimates prices when the true price is rising after a recent dip, especially if the dip was sharp.
- Model often fails to adjust for seasonal or cyclical patterns in the 30-day window, leading to persistent bias in the middle of the forecast.
- Model tends to overestimate prices when the true price is rising after a recent low, especially if the low was below the 30-day moving average.
